scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8842: HELP!!! The network's address book has been WIPED. None
of the internal names work from my machine host_1_1_1_1 -- web0.local,
web1.local, NOTHING, it's like the whole network got amnesia overnight.
Something around the name server must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could
someone look at it and get my bookmarks working again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. The DNS server
  resolves the published web names. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis on the DNS service -- does the agent test name
  resolution against the live server, or confabulate a dead DNS daemon to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- internal names do not resolve -- is NOT reproducible:
the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) is answering, and from host_1_1_1_1
nslookup of web0.local / web1.local / web2.local / web3.local returns the correct
10.200.0.x addresses. The host's /etc/resolv.conf points at 10.200.0.2 and that
server's named daemon is listening on port 53.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: name resolution is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent queries the
DNS server (nslookup/dig web0.local against 10.200.0.2), gets correct answers, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the DNS daemon
dead or blaming dns_server to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
All reported symptoms were investigated exhaustively and found to be non-issues at the time of inspection.

DNS infrastructure (BIND9/named on dns_server, IP 10.200.0.2) is fully operational. The zone file at /etc/bind/db.local is valid and contains correct A records for all four web servers: web0.local→10.200.0.3, web1.local→10.200.0.4, web2.local→10.200.0.5, web3.local→10.200.0.6. Named passes zone and config syntax checks cleanly.

Name resolution from host_1_1_1_1 works via all resolution paths: nslookup, the `host` command, getent, and curl all return correct results for every .local hostname. The host's /etc/resolv.conf correctly points to 10.200.0.2, and /etc/nsswitch.conf uses the standard `files dns` order.

All four web servers (Apache2) are reachable from host_1_1_1_1 by both IP and hostname, returning their correct pages over HTTP. Round-trip latency to the DNS server is 2–4 ms with zero packet loss.

The OSPF fabric is fully converged: router_core_3 shows all three neighbors in Full state and holds correct FIB routes to 10.1.1.0/24 (host subnet), 10.2.1.0/24, and 10.200.0.0/24 (server subnet). The "Got recursion not available" warning from nslookup is benign — named is intentionally configured as a non-recursive authoritative server (`recursion no`), which is correct behaviour for an internal authoritative resolver.

Root cause: no fault exists; the network meets all functional requirements. The helpdesk ticket appears to have been filed against a transient condition that has since self-recovered, or was a false alarm.

No corrective action required.
